title: Non-geometrically reduced fibres near a non-geometrically reduced generic fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $Y$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and suppose the generic fibre $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is not geometrically reduced over $\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $V\subseteq Y$ such that for every $y\in V$, the fibre $X_y$ is not geometrically reduced over $\kappa(y)$. No flatness, reducedness of $Y$, Noetherianity, or nonemptiness of the fibres is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-generic-geometrically-reduced-preparation] to $f$. Obtain a nonempty open $U\subseteq Y$, an integral affine scheme $T$, a finite universal homeomorphism $q:T\to U$, and $R=(X\times_YT)_{\mathrm{red}}$ whose generic fibre is geometrically reduced. Put $P=X\times_YT$ and let $h:P\to T$ be the projection. The base change $h$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change] and quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], hence finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. An integral scheme is irreducible by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $\xi$ be its generic point. The homeomorphism $q$ maps $\xi$ to $\eta$: $q(\xi)$ is generic in $U$, and $U$ is a nonempty open of irreducible $Y$, hence dense, so the closure of $q(\xi)$ in $Y$ is $Y$; thus $q(\xi)$ and $\eta$ are generic points of the irreducible closed subset $Y$, which are equal by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Here the homeomorphism assertion is the identity base change in [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism].

source.place: Tag 0577, application of Tag 0550 and its diagram

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change] to $f$ and the composite $T\xrightarrow{q}U\hookrightarrow Y$. It says that the geometric fibre of $h$ at $\xi$ is reduced if and only if the geometric fibre of $f$ at $\eta$ is reduced. By [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-algebraic-closure-test], these conditions are respectively geometric reducedness of $P_\xi$ and of $X_\eta$. The latter fails by hypothesis. Therefore $P_\xi$ is not geometrically reduced. This uses the algebraic-closure criterion explicitly because the fibre-locus node is stated in terms of reduced geometric fibres.

source.place: Tag 0577, generic-fibre comparison using Tag 0576 (and Varieties 035X)

proof.text: By [lem-pur-reduction-generic-fibre] applied to $h:P\to T$, the scheme $R_\xi=(P_{\mathrm{red}})_\xi$ is canonically $(P_\xi)_{\mathrm{red}}$. If $P_\xi$ were reduced, this reduction map would be an isomorphism: on each affine its map is the quotient by the zero nilradical [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. But $R_\xi$ is geometrically reduced by step 1, whereas $P_\xi$ is not by step 2. This contradiction shows that $P_\xi$ is not reduced.

source.place: Tag 0577, reduction morphism and nonreduced generic fibre

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nonreduced-fibre-open] to $h:P\to T$. Its hypotheses hold: $h$ is finite type and $T$ irreducible with generic point $\xi$ by step 1, and $P_\xi$ is not reduced by step 3. Obtain a nonempty open $W\subseteq T$ such that $P_t$ is not reduced for every $t\in W$.

Set $V=q(W)\subseteq U$. Because $q$ is a homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism], $V$ is nonempty and open in $U$, hence open in $Y$. For $y\in V$ choose $t\in W$ with $q(t)=y$. The fibre-product universal property and [def-pc-scheme-fibre] give $P_t\cong X_y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$: both objects represent pairs of a map to $X$ and a map to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ commuting over $Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $X_y$ were geometrically reduced, this base change would be reduced by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], contrary to step 4. Thus $X_y$ is not geometrically reduced for every $y\in V$, as required.
